## Geometric Brownian Motion Definition
A Geometric Brownian Motion $(S_{t})$ has dynamics given by the
[[stochastic-calculus|stochastic differential equation]]
$$
dS_{t}=\mu S_{t}dt+\sigma S_tdW_t,
$$
where $W_{t}$ is [[brownian-motion]] and $\mu, \sigma$ are constants.

## Solution
To solve the SDE consider the ansatz $g(S_{t})=\log S_t$. Then by
[[ito-formula]] we have that
$$
dg(S_t)=d\log(S_t)=\frac{1}{S_{t}}dS_t+\frac12\frac{1}{S_{t}^{2}}dS_t^2=\frac{1}{S_{t}}dS_t+\frac12\sigma^2dt
$$
If we substitute in our initial expression we obtain
$$
\begin{align}
d\log(S_{t})=\frac1{S_{t}}(\mu S_tdt+\sigma S_tdW_{t})+\frac12\sigma^2dt=\left(\mu+\frac12\sigma^{2}\right)dt+\sigma dW_t.
\end{align}
$$
Written in integral form we have
$$
\begin{align}
\log S_{t}&=\log S_0+\left(\mu+\frac12\sigma^{2}\right)t+\sigma W_t\\
\implies S_t&=S_0\exp\left(\left(\mu-\frac{1}{2}\sigma^2\right)t+\sigma W_t\right)
\end{align}
$$
## Variants of Geometric Brownian Motion
### Mean-Reverting GBM ([[ornstein-uhlenbeck-process]])
Instead of constant drift, the drift term reverts toward a long-term mean:
$$
dS_t = \kappa(\mu - \log S_t)S_t dt + \sigma S_t dW_t
$$
Used for interest rates and commodity prices that have equilibrium levels.

### [[local-volatility-models]]
Volatility is a function of both time and price: $\sigma = \sigma(t, S_t)$
$$
dS_t = \mu S_t dt + \sigma(t, S_t) S_t dW_t
$$
Allows fitting to observed option prices more accurately than constant
volatility.

### [[stochastic-volatility-models]]
Volatility itself follows a random process (e.g., [[heston-model]]):
$$
dS_t = \mu S_t dt + \sqrt{v_t} S_t dW_t^S
$$
$$
dv_t = \kappa(\theta - v_t) dt + \xi\sqrt{v_t} dW_t^v
$$
Can capture smile effects and time-varying volatility.

### [[jump-diffusion-models-merton-model]]
Adds random jump component to GBM:
$$
dS_t = \mu S_t dt + \sigma S_t dW_t + S_t d\left(\sum_{i=1}^{N_t} (J_i - 1)\right)
$$
Where $N_t$ is a Poisson process and $J_i$ are jump magnitudes. Captures tail
risk.

### [[cev-model-constant-elasticity-of-variance]]
Volatility scales with price level: $\sigma(S_t) = \sigma S_t^{\beta-1}$
$$
dS_t = \mu S_t dt + \sigma S_t^\beta dW_t
$$
When $\beta < 1$, exhibits volatility smile observed in options markets.

### [[displaced-diffusion]]
Combines GBM with an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck component for short rates.
